title: Domain NFT Owners Can Review and Revoke Token Approvals

cover.subtitle: Verify the permission that the contract records.
cover.visual: A tiny domain token card and a small operator permission switch set to off. No private keys, wallet addresses or numeric claims.

sections.name: 01-token-approvals-and-operator-approvals-grant-different-scope
sections.heading: Token approvals and operator approvals grant different scope
sections.scene: One token card has one approved address. A separate operator bracket covers three token cards within one contract boundary. Another contract stays outside.
sections.alt: Token approvals and operator approvals grant different scope.

sections.name: 02-a-review-identifies-the-exact-asset-and-current-permission
sections.heading: A review identifies the exact asset and current permission
sections.scene: Chain, contract, token ID, owner, and operator fields form a review checklist beside contract-read results. No real wallet addresses or brand logos.
sections.alt: A review identifies the exact asset and current permission.

sections.name: 03-revocation-must-change-the-intended-contract-state
sections.heading: Revocation must change the intended contract state
sections.scene: A transaction card reads setApprovalForAll(operator,false), then confirmed state reads false. A wallet-disconnect icon sits separately, without a revocation checkmark.
sections.alt: Revocation must change the intended contract state.

sections.name: 04-cleanup-and-incident-recovery-require-separate-follow-up
sections.heading: Cleanup and incident recovery require separate follow-up
sections.scene: Two paths separate routine unused-approval removal from compromised-key recovery. Domain DNS, account access, and token ownership receive separate final checks.
sections.alt: Cleanup and incident recovery require separate follow-up.

purpose: Initial illustration plan. The final image review manifest records actual asset hashes and visual revisions.
